exact_statement: For Theta uniform on [0,2*pi), set psi6(x)=exp(6*i*Theta) for every x. The field law is rotation invariant, E[psi6(x)]=0, but E[psi6(x)*conj(psi6(y))]=1 for every x,y. Hence a vanishing one-point hexatic order parameter does not imply absence of long-range orientational correlations.
assumptions: One common uniform angle is used at every point; this is an auxiliary field, not a positive-temperature Riesz Gibbs state.
proof: The uniform-angle integral of exp(6*i*Theta) is zero. The product with its conjugate is identically one. Adding a deterministic angle preserves the uniform law.
remaining_gap: No microscopic Riesz-to-elastic, defect-sector, or real particle/bond correlation comparison; no proof or refutation of P0321.
target_relation: Counterexample to the stronger auxiliary implication, not to P0321.
prior_work_status: Independent reproduction of at-p0321; not new and not included in the new brain draft.

exact_statement: Let T,mu,a,Lambda>0, G!=0 in R^2, 0<=p<=2, and let a centered real Gaussian displacement field modulo constants have spectral covariance T*(P_T/(mu*|k|^2)+P_L/(a*|k|^p))*1_{0<|k|<Lambda} with Fourier measure d^2k/(2*pi)^2. For fixed unit e, C_G(r*e)=E exp(i*G.(u(r*e)-u(0))) has a positive finite prefactor times r^{-T*|G|^2/(4*pi*mu)}(1+o(1)) if p<2; at p=2 the exponent gains T*|G|^2/(4*pi*a). For theta=curl(u)/2, E exp(6*i*(theta(x)-theta(0))) tends to exp(-9*T*Lambda^2/(4*pi*mu))>0. Exponential positional decay and decaying orientational correlations are impossible in this specified Gaussian proxy model.
assumptions: Sharp ultraviolet cutoff Lambda; infrared limit taken on anchored increments.
Positive fixed coefficients; G nonzero; p fixed for the distance limit.
The proxy theta is not identified with a microscopic bond observable; no defects or nonlinear Gibbs approximation assumed.
proof: Exact Gaussian characteristic function; polar reduction to F(z)=integral_0^z(1-cos(t))/t dt; angular dominated convergence with integrable |log|cos(phi)||; integrable longitudinal spectrum for p<2; analogous angular argument for p=2; curl projects out longitudinal spectrum and Riemann-Lebesgue gives its limiting pair correlation.
remaining_gap: No microscopic Riesz-to-elastic, defect-sector, or real particle/bond correlation comparison; no proof or refutation of P0321.
target_relation: Limits the defect-free harmonic route only; does not refute P0321.

exact_statement: Under C002 assumptions, define L(p,r)=-log(C_G,p(r*e))/log(r), r>1. Then lim_{p->2-}lim_{r->infinity}L(p,r)=T*|G|^2/(4*pi*mu), whereas lim_{r->infinity}lim_{p->2-}L(p,r)=T*|G|^2/(4*pi*mu)+T*|G|^2/(4*pi*a). Thus the fixed-p exponent convergence is not uniform over p<2.
assumptions: Exactly the cutoff Gaussian spectral family of C002.
Fixed positive T,mu,a,Lambda and fixed nonzero G, unit e.
proof: C002 supplies the distance limits. At finite r, continuity in p at 2 follows by dominated convergence using the integrable increment-weighted |k|^{-2} kernel. Positivity of the extra endpoint exponent separates the iterated limits.
remaining_gap: No microscopic Riesz-to-elastic, defect-sector, or real particle/bond correlation comparison; no proof or refutation of P0321.
target_relation: Counterexample to interchanging these auxiliary endpoint and thermodynamic-distance limits, not to existence of a hexatic Gibbs phase.

exact_statement: w546 L01 is correct for a centered stationary real Gaussian field with even nonnegative L1 spectral density and real nonzero m: its exponential increment correlation tends to exp(-m^2 R(0))>0.
assumptions: Exactly the L1 stationary Gaussian assumptions in AUDIT_W546_L01.md; m real nonzero.
proof: Exact Gaussian increment variance and characteristic function, followed by the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma. Independent curl special case saved before peer proof was read.
